summary.text: 国 means “country” and is a simplified form of 國. Its outer enclosure survives from the older form, but 玉 has replaced the inner 或. To understand the character historically, keep that replacement in view: the older enclosure marked territory and 或 provided sound.

formation.text: An older meaning-and-sound compound has undergone component replacement. 國 combines enclosure and phonetic 或; 国 substitutes 玉, concealing that sound relationship.

components.text: The surrounding enclosure marks a bounded area or territory. It survives in both 國 and 国.
玉 occupies the position of the older phonetic 或. Its ordinary meaning “jade” can support a memory aid for 国, but does not explain the older formation of 國.

history.text: 或 could itself write the country or territory word before the fuller enclosed form became established. 國 is attested in Western Zhou writing, with the added enclosure making the territorial meaning explicit. Later enclosure variants preserve that function.

In an Old Chinese reconstruction, 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ have closely matching sounds, which helps explain 或 as the phonetic. The modern replacement 玉 preserves neither that written component nor its visible link with 國’s reconstructed pronunciation.

国 is also the modern Japanese form corresponding to 國. The change concerns the written shape of the country character; it does not make “jade within borders” the ancient origin of either written tradition.
